page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E4.Flex.64-1024 is an x86_64 virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7J13 processor operating at a base clock speed of 2.55 GHz. The virtual configuration allocates 64 dedicated physical cores supporting 128 vCPUs across two threads per core, combined with 1024 GB of system memory. Cache hierarchy details include 64 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AES, VAES, SHA_NI, and BMI2, while AVX-512 and AMX instructions are unsupported. The server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address and bundles neither local NVMe storage nor dedicated GPU hardware, requiring persistent data to be attached via network storage.

Benchmark results highlight exceptional parallel execution capabilities, placing the instance in the top tier for multi-threaded processing. It delivers a multi-core score of 171,639.87 on stress-ng and achieves 587.81 GB/sec on multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Single-threaded computing remains strong at 2,682.59 in stress-ng. Memory subsystems demonstrate high cached performance with 7,154.28 GB/sec in small 16 KB block reads, transitioning to 137.86 GB/sec read and 67.75 GB/sec write bandwidth on large 256 MB uncached transfers. Application-level testing reflects solid throughput, handling 104.72 million Redis SET operations per second and 53.58 GB/sec in static web serving. On CPU-based language model prompt processing, the system sustains 4,044.43 tokens per second on 135M parameter models and 192.39 tokens per second on 7B models.

The 8 GB per vCPU allocation provides substantial memory density alongside high core counts, yielding favorable cost efficiency for memory-intensive parallel workloads compared to higher-tier bare-metal servers. The primary tradeoff stems from the absence of integrated local NVMe storage, meaning disk-bound operations depend on remote block volume performance. Furthermore, workloads requiring AVX-512 or hardware matrix acceleration must rely on alternative architectures. VM.Standard.E4.Flex.64-1024 is functionally targeted at large-scale in-memory databases, distributed Redis clusters, enterprise caching layers, heavy parallel ETL workflows, and large multi-threaded application servers.
